prologue.title: The Village of Twiggle
prologue.narrator: Sometimes days go by so fast that we forget to live them.
prologue.text:
You arrive in the village of Twiggle with your friend Aikito.

Aikito is a curious little dog who loves to play, chase leaves and cars, and ask far too many questions.

But today, something is strange.

The villagers are running everywhere.

Everyone keeps saying:

“Quick!”
“No time!”
“Later!”

Even the children have stopped playing.

Far away, a huge tick-tock echoes from the hill.

Aikito sniffs the air and scrunches up his tiny eyebrows.

*“It smells weird... like when you're late for something you never planned.”*

choices.text: Follow the sound with Aikito
Stay and play with the children

jeu.title: Five More Minutes
jeu.narrator: Sometimes playing matters more than hurrying.
jeu.text:
You suggest a game of ball.

At first, nobody dares.

Then Aikito catches the ball with his head and tumbles into a puddle.

Everyone bursts out laughing.

Even the grown-ups stop for a few seconds.

The ticking seems to slow down a little.

A little girl with red hair comes up to you.

*“What's your dog? Does he always do stuff like that?”*

Aikito shakes his head and splashes water everywhere. Everyone laughs even harder.

choices.text: Play a little longer with the little girl
Climb the hill with Aikito

nouvelle_amie.title: Léonie
nouvelle_amie.narrator: A new friendship often starts with a fit of giggles.
nouvelle_amie.text:
Her name is Léonie. She has always lived in Twiggle.

*“We used to play here all the time,”* she says. *“And then the clock started going too fast. Now everyone is in a hurry, and nobody has time for anything.”*

Aikito sits down in front of her and tilts his head.

*“Even the butterflies go faster,”* he says seriously. *“I tried to catch one this morning. It was already gone before I finished waking up.”*

Léonie laughs.

*“Your dog talks?”*

*“Only when it's important,”* you reply.

choices.text: Ask Léonie what's on the hill
Climb the hill together

leonie_raconte.title: What Léonie Knows
leonie_raconte.narrator: Children often notice things that grown-ups have stopped seeing.
leonie_raconte.text:
Léonie sits down on a bench. She speaks softly.

*“The clock showed up three weeks ago. At first, you could barely hear it. And then people started checking the time all the time. And then running. And then forgetting to eat, to laugh, to look at the sky.”*

She stares at her shoes.

*“My dad stopped telling me stories at night. He says he doesn't have time anymore. But at night... the time is still there. He just doesn't see it anymore.”*

Aikito rests his head on Léonie's knees.

*“Your dad needs us to give him his time back,”* he says.

choices.text: Climb the hill with Léonie and Aikito

chemin_colline.title: The Path to the Hill
chemin_colline.location: PATH — BETWEEN THE VILLAGE AND THE HILL
chemin_colline.narrator: The path up the hill is full of things to look at, if you take the time.
chemin_colline.text:
The path climbs gently.

Aikito stops every two minutes to sniff something.

*“A snail came through here this morning,”* he says. *“It was going the wrong way. I didn't tell it. I didn't want to hurt its feelings.”*

You look back at the village below. People are still running. One man is in such a hurry that he forgets his hat. He goes back for his hat and forgets his basket. He goes back for his basket and...

*“They forget things because they go too fast,”* says Aikito. *“If you go too fast, you leave little pieces of yourself behind along the way.”*

choices.text: Keep going to the top
Stop and watch a cloud with Aikito

chemin_colline_amis.title: The Path for Three
chemin_colline_amis.location: PATH — BETWEEN THE VILLAGE AND THE HILL
chemin_colline_amis.narrator: Paths are nicer when you share them.
chemin_colline_amis.text:
Léonie walks beside you. Aikito runs ahead, comes back, and runs off again.

He picks up a leaf and solemnly lays it at Léonie's feet.

*“This is for you,”* he says. *“It fell from the tree at exactly the right moment.”*

Léonie laughs and picks up the leaf.

*“How does he know it was the right moment?”*

*“I don't know,”* you say. *“Aikito says a lot of things that sound like they make no sense at all, and somehow they always end up making sense.”*

Aikito nods with great dignity.

choices.text: Keep going to the top

nuage.title: The Dog-Shaped Cloud
nuage.narrator: Watching the clouds is one of the most important things you can do.
nuage.text:
You both stretch out in the grass.

Aikito points his muzzle at the sky.

*“That one looks like a dog chasing a ball,”* he says.

You look. He's right.

*“And that one looks like a hat that lost its owner,”* you add.

You stay there for a while. The ticking of the clock is still there, but from far away it almost sounds like music.

*“I wonder if the clock is sad,”* says Aikito. *“Going so fast all the time. I would be sad.”*

You had never thought of it that way.

choices.text: Climb up to see the clock up close

colline.title: The Giant Clock
colline.narrator: Some clocks tell the time. Others set the pace of the world.
colline.text:
You and Aikito reach the top of the hill.

An immense clock is turning far too fast.

With every tick:
- the grown-ups run faster,
- the children put their toys away,
- the sun seems to race across the sky.

Aikito looks up at you.

*“Maybe the villagers forgot to take their time…”*

Up close, the clock is covered in tiny carvings: children playing, grown-ups laughing, families eating together.

*“It used to be beautiful,”* Aikito says softly. *“I can feel it.”*

choices.text: Sit calmly with Aikito
Try to stop the clock
Look at the carvings more closely

gravures_horloge.title: What the Clock Remembers
gravures_horloge.location: HILL OF MINUTES — AT THE CLOCK'S BASE
gravures_horloge.narrator: Old objects keep the memory of what they have seen.
gravures_horloge.text:
You step closer and rest your fingers on the carvings.

Children running through meadows. An old man fishing. A mother reading a story. A dad looking at the stars with his little girl.

*“It remembers,”* says Aikito. *“The clock remembers when time was gentle.”*

You watch the hands spinning at top speed. They seem almost... out of breath.

*“I think someone told it to go faster one day,”* says Aikito. *“And it obeyed. But nobody ever told it to stop.”*

That gives you an idea.

choices.text: Speak softly to the clock
Sit down and set an example

parler_horloge.title: A Conversation with Time
parler_horloge.narrator: You can talk to anything, if you put your heart into it.
parler_horloge.text:
You place your hand on the clock's warm wood.

*“You can slow down,”* you say softly. *“Nobody needs to go this fast. The people down there forgot to look at the sky. They forgot to laugh. They need time.”*

Aikito adds, very seriously:

*“And I need time to catch butterflies.”*

The clock doesn't answer. But something changes: the ticking is a tiny bit softer.

Not enough yet. But a little.

choices.text: Sit with Aikito and stay calm
Go back down to the village with Léonie

sasseoir.title: Sitting Down
sasseoir.narrator: Sometimes the bravest thing is to refuse to hurry.
sasseoir.text:
You both sit down in the grass, facing the clock.

Aikito yawns and rests his head on your knees.

The hands keep spinning fast.

But the two of you don't move.

A bird lands nearby. Then another. Even the birds seem intrigued by two beings who refuse to hurry.

*“I think the clock is watching us,”* Aikito whispers.

You look at the hands. Maybe he's right.

They seem... to hesitate.

choices.text: Stay a little longer, doing nothing
Go back down to the village with Léonie

arreter_horloge.title: Aikito's Plan
arreter_horloge.narrator: Big plans often start with small ideas.
arreter_horloge.text:
You walk up to the clock. It's enormous, its gears grinding and rumbling.

Aikito thinks it over, paws crossed.

*“I could bite a gear,”* he suggests.

*“No.”*

*“I could sit on it.”*

*“No.”*

*“We could sing really loudly until it stops out of embarrassment?”*

You look at Aikito. He is completely serious.

*“I have a better idea,”* you say.

choices.text: Share your idea with Aikito

idee_cle.title: The Key to Time
idee_cle.narrator: The right idea always arrives at the right moment.
idee_cle.text:
*“What if we don't try to stop it? What if we just show it... what calm looks like?”*

Aikito tilts his head.

*“Like an example?”*

*“Like an example.”*

The two of you sit down in the grass, facing the immense clock.

Aikito pulls a ball out of nowhere and bounces it gently. Once. Twice. Slowly.

You look up at the sky.

The hands hesitate.

choices.text: Stay calm together
Go back down to the village with Léonie

fin_douce.title: Time to Play
fin_douce.narrator: Some things need time to become beautiful.
fin_douce.text:
You and Aikito watch the sun set.

The clock slowly settles into a gentler rhythm.

Down in the village, the children start playing again.

The grown-ups finally stop running.

Aikito wags his tail, then says softly:

*“Grown-ups sometimes forget to play.*
*But I don't want to forget.”*

You look down at Twiggle. Laughter drifts up to you, light as soap bubbles.

The clock keeps ticking. But now it's keeping a good pace. Not too fast. Not too slow.

Just... the time it needs.

fin_amis.title: Evening in Twiggle
fin_amis.narrator: The best days are the ones you hadn't planned.
fin_amis.text:
The sun sinks over Twiggle.

The clock has slowed down. The laughter has come back.

Léonie runs to her father, who is waiting for her at the front door.

He crouches down, opens his arms, and this time... he doesn't look at the time.

Aikito nudges you with his muzzle.

*“See? He found his time again.”*

In the sky, the first stars appear.

*“There's a star for every moment you take the time to live,”* says Aikito.

*“Is that true?”*

*“I don't know. But it's nice to believe.”*
